question: Which part of a lithium-ion cell is meant to melt on purpose when it overheats?
answer: The separator, the plastic film between the electrodes. Thinner than a hair, it is often polypropylene outside and polyethylene inside. At about 130 °C the polyethylene softens and seals the pores ions travel through, cutting the current, while the polypropylene, melting near 165 °C, holds the film together. The fuse is carrier-bag plastic.
move: Good safety parts are designed to fail in one chosen way.
reference: Arora & Zhang, Battery Separators, Chemical Reviews, 2004
